sections.h2: Where in Morehead do I handle a Rowan County tax bill?
sections.html:
The PVA and the sheriff both operate from the Rowan County Courthouse at 600 West Main Street, open weekdays from 8 AM to 4 PM. The PVA, at (606) 784-5512, assesses all taxable real and personal property, tracks changes of ownership, keeps parcel maps and processes exemptions. The sheriff, at (606) 784-5446, mails and collects the bills.

The county's property tax page says the sheriff takes cash, checks and money orders in person, and accepts cards through an outside vendor that charges 2.49 percent on amounts above $60 and a flat $1.50 below that. An online option also exists for anyone with a bill number ready.

When a bill goes delinquent, the County Clerk and the County Attorney step in, and the county's delinquent taxes page explains how they work alongside the sheriff.

sections.h2: What is Rowan County's own payment calendar?
sections.html:
Rowan County publishes a discount window that closes on November 30, later than the usual November 1 cutoff, and says bills first go out at the start of November.

Rowan County, KY: stages for a sheriff's property tax bill, per the county
StageWhat applies
Before November 302 percent discount
By December 31Face amount of the bill
January 1 to January 315 percent penalty
February 1 to April 1521 percent total penalty
After April 15Delinquent, handed to the County Clerk

A late mailing lets the Department of Revenue shift the calendar under KRS 134.015, so dates can move from one year to the next. Since the debt attaches to whoever held title on January 1, a spring seller should plan on settling the year's bill.

sections.h2: What would a median Rowan County house owe the state?
sections.html:
The state set 2025 at 10.6 cents for each hundred dollars of assessment. With QuickFacts listing a typical Rowan County home at $161,800, the state's share lands near $171.51. Other taxing bodies stack their rates on it, and the sheriff can quote a combined figure for any address.

Owners from age 65, and owners who are totally disabled, subtract $49,100 across 2025 and 2026. That leaves $112,700 taxable on the typical home and a state share near $119.46. Apply with the PVA at the courthouse, bringing a license or passport.

Only 61.5 percent of Rowan County homes are occupied by owners, so many parcels are rentals. A landlord who sells will be asked who covers the year's bill.

sections.h2: How does Rowan County pursue delinquent taxes?
sections.html:
After April 15 the bill rests with the County Clerk, and the county attorney follows a published timetable. Two letters go out on set dates, and the sale usually lands in mid August.

  • May 15: the County Attorney mails a 30-day notice.
  • June 15: a 60-day notice follows for bills still open.
  • Second week of August: the customary sale, where outside investors may buy a bill and add fees.
  • Each month: the delinquent amount climbs by 1 percent until it is paid.

The owner of record can sign a delinquent tax contract with the County Attorney's office up to three days before the sale. The county requires 10 percent of the bill that day and spreads the rest over monthly payments. A contract signed ahead of the clerk's sale keeps investors from buying the bill.

The County Attorney also presses the county's tax claim in foreclosure cases, where it holds priority.

sections.h2: How can a Rowan County owner contest a valuation?
sections.html:
The first step is a mandatory sit-down with the PVA or a deputy. Inspection of the roll runs thirteen days beginning May's first Monday, with the dates and appeal instructions advertised in the county's largest newspaper. At the sit-down the PVA explains how your figure was built and writes it up.

  • File the appeal with the clerk on the workday after viewing ends.
  • Prepare evidence: land and building descriptions, policies, construction costs, listings or sales. A case without any is rejected.
  • The hearing comes roughly a month after viewing, before a panel of local owners.
  • A hired agent must come from a statutory group, among them attorneys, CPAs and licensed appraisers.

Bills printed before a ruling use your claimed value, and a supplemental bill follows if the board lands higher.

sections.h2: Does selling a Rowan County house clear back taxes?
sections.html:
It does not. KRS 134.420 puts a lien on the parcel once taxes turn delinquent, and the lien lasts eleven years under any owner. A title search at the County Clerk reveals it, and it is normally paid off at closing.

A Department of Revenue example shows how fast debt grows after April 15. A $1,000 bill becomes $1,254.00 on transfer, about $1,387.79 inside five business days and $1,611.30 after the county attorney's first notice, before another month of interest. Paying the sheriff on time avoids that.

An owner who is behind has three routes before the August sale: pay the sheriff, pay the clerk, or sign a contract with the County Attorney. A direct cash sale is a fourth when repairs or inherited debts stand in the way, with the balance taken out of the proceeds.

sections.h2: What does a seller gain from knowing Rowan County's background?
sections.html:
Parts of Fleming and Morgan counties became Rowan County in 1856, in the Eastern Kentucky Coalfield, with about 280 square miles of land. Morehead is the seat and Lakeview Heights the other city. Morehead was incorporated in 1869, holds close to 7,000 people, and hosts Morehead State University, Cave Run Lake, Rowan County Senior High School and St. Claire Healthcare, which the city says employs 1,200. Lewis, Carter, Elliott, Morgan, Menifee, Bath and Fleming counties adjoin it, and part of the Daniel Boone National Forest falls inside the line.

The county's early story shapes today's map. Surveyors from Pennsylvania are believed to have explored the area in 1773, and the first settlement grew at Farmers, about ten miles west of Morehead. Clearfield came second and had the first sawmill in the county. Morehead, third in line, was founded in 1854 by a colonel who bought the land and named the town for a governor. A tax levied on Morehead in 1896 paid for hard-surfaced roads, and that road system reached Farmers by 1920.

Census QuickFacts supplies these housing figures:

  • July 2025 population estimate of 24,476, which is 0.7 percent under 2020.
  • Owners occupy 61.5 percent of homes, across 9,592 households averaging 2.25 people.
  • Typical home value $161,800; typical gross rent $825.
  • Household income at the midpoint is $54,321, and a quarter of adults (25.9 percent) have a bachelor's degree.
  • Eight building permits in 2025, and broadband in 93.4 percent of households.

The 2020 census measured a median age of 32.7 and counted 10,518 housing units, of which 13.2 percent stood vacant. Of the occupied units, 62.3 percent were owner-occupied and 37.7 percent rented, with 38 percent of residents in urban areas and 62 percent rural. New construction is thin, so most listings are existing houses.

faqs.q: When does the Rowan County discount end?
faqs.a: The county lists a 2 percent discount for bills paid before November 30. The printed amount is then due through December 31, and 5 percent is added in January.

faqs.q: Can I pay the Rowan County sheriff by card?
faqs.a: Yes: Visa, MasterCard, American Express and Discover, through a vendor that charges 2.49 percent above $60 or $1.50 below it. Cash, checks and money orders are welcome too.

faqs.q: How do I contact the Rowan County sheriff's office?
faqs.a: Call (606) 784-5446 or visit 600 West Main Street in Morehead, weekdays 8 AM to 4 PM.

faqs.q: Is a payment plan possible once a Rowan County bill is delinquent?
faqs.a: Yes, through the County Attorney's office: 10 percent of the bill is due on signing day and the remainder is split into monthly payments. Sign before the sale to keep investors out.

faqs.q: Who handles questions about a Rowan County valuation?
faqs.a: The Property Valuation Administrator, at (606) 784-5512. A conference there comes before any appeal at the County Clerk.
